basic_info.name: InsideTracker (Segterra, Inc.)
basic_info.category: Personalized health analytics platform — hybrid of direct-to-consumer lab testing + proprietary biomarker interpretation engine ('precision wellness'). Now also a B2B AI platform (Terra) licensing its engine to wellness brands.
basic_info.country: United States (HQ Cambridge, MA). Testing via 2,500+ Quest Diagnostics locations; mobile phlebotomy required in NY/NJ/RI/HI/AZ and Canada; 'Blood Results Upload' sold internationally. No presence in Brazil.
basic_info.stage: Private, growth-stage. Founded 2009 (~17 years old); $15M Series B (2022) led by BASF Venture Capital (~$17.5-19M total raised); no disclosed valuation or exit. 2025-2026 signals strategic pivot from consumer brand toward B2B AI platform (Terra launch May 2026; Ultrahuman partnership Jan 2025; CEO Rony Sellam, succeeding founder Gil Blander).
basic_info.pricing_model: Cash-pay one-time kits + repurchase loop (no insurance; HSA/FSA eligible): Ultimate (48 biomarkers, blood draw) $489-699 depending on source/promo; InnerAge 2.0 add-on $249 standalone ($99 bundled with Ultimate); DNA Kit $249 (261 variants); Blood Results Upload $119 (analyze existing labs from any CLIA lab); DNA Results Upload $29; mobile phlebotomy +$99; membership renewal ~$149/yr; multi-packs (2x Ultimate+2x InnerAge $1,388; 4x $2,681). Cheaper Home/Essentials kits were discontinued — entry price rose. [uncertain: exact current SKUs/promos vary by source]
basic_info.target_user: Health-optimization consumers 18+: athletes, biohackers, longevity-focused professionals (user base skews ~85% white, active, normal BMI, age 40-43). Secondary: B2B buyers — pro/collegiate sports, US military, gym chains, wearable brands (Oura, Ultrahuman).
basic_info.scale_metrics: Funding ~$17.5-19M total (Series B $15M, 2022, BASF VC + OurCrowd/PeakBridge/BAMCAP etc.); valuation undisclosed [uncertain]. User counts never officially disclosed — research cohorts cover 20,000-28,000 users (PLOS studies), marketing claims 'exponential growth' after Series B and a proprietary database of 10B+ data points across tens of thousands of users [uncertain]. Durable-threat signals: 17 years of accumulated longitudinal biomarker data, 3 peer-reviewed (company-authored) outcome studies, patents (US 8762167), Harvard/MIT/Tufts founding team, and B2B distribution via sports/military/wearable partnerships. Noise: funding is small vs. category winners; consumer pricing limits mass-market reach.

product.core_features: Blood panels (up to 48 biomarkers via Quest or mobile draw); InnerAge 2.0 biological-age score (13-14 biomarkers women / 17-18 men, weighted by age-correlation); DNA analysis (261 variants); Blood/DNA Results Upload (interpret existing data); personalized Optimal Zones per biomarker (age/sex/athlete-adjusted vs lab reference ranges); Action Plan engine (choose 1-5 goals -> filtered from 7,500+ food/supplement/exercise/lifestyle actions, each linked to cited studies); recipes/meal planning; Nutrition DeepDive food+supplement tracker (2024); 'Ask InsideTracker' AI chat (2024); wearable data ingestion (Apple Health, Fitbit, Garmin, Oura — all read-only, one-way in); goal tracking with reminders via app/text/email; retest cadence recommended every 3 months.
product.signature_differentiator: The 'Optimal Zone' thesis, executed end-to-end: for every biomarker InsideTracker computes a personalized optimal band (adjusted by age, biological sex, activity level) instead of accepting the lab's population 'normal range' — then plots the user against that band, converts every out-of-zone marker into cited, prioritized lifestyle actions, and proves the loop with retrospective outcome studies (43 biomarkers improved in 20k-user cohort over 4 years). InnerAge 2.0 compresses this into one aspirational number (biological age) computed by ML over its own dataset of health-conscious users — explicitly NOT sick-population reference data. No competitor combines: own biomarker database + own optimal-zone engine + own action engine + published (albeit self-authored) outcome data. The May 2026 Terra platform productizes this engine as 'neurosymbolic' AI (deep learning + symbolic rules over 7,000+ curated studies) for B2B buyers — the 'hallucination-free personalized guidance' pitch.
product.lab_data_handling: Two ingestion paths: (1) buy a panel -> activate -> print lab order -> venous draw at Quest (Ultimate = ~6 vials, results in 5-7 business days) or +$99 mobile phlebotomist at home/office (mandatory in NY/NJ/RI/HI/AZ/Canada); (2) Blood Results Upload ($119) — send results from any recent blood test, interpreted against InsideTracker's zones (only markers in their system). No LIS integration, no lab partnership API for consumers; Quest is the fulfillment lab. Cadence: company recommends retesting every ~3 months (drives repurchase); wearables stream continuous sleep/activity data between tests. No at-home fingerprick anymore (Home/Essentials kits discontinued); no CGM product.
product.family_dependents_depth: None. Strictly single-user accounts, 18+ only, no dependent profiles, no caregiver mode, no pediatric ranges, no hereditary-risk family view. Closest artifact is multi-pack SKUs (2x/4x Ultimate+InnerAge bundles) that a couple/family could buy, but each kit is a separate adult account with zero cross-account tooling. Confirmed gap — and notably InsideTracker's own DNA product gives propensity info without family linkage.
product.doctor_sharing: Minimal, patient-initiated: support docs confirm you can share/download results with your doctor or nutritionist (persisting even after membership lapses), with an official how-to video; framing is 'discuss with your provider — InsideTracker is not a substitute for a licensed medical professional.' No structured consultation brief, no SOAP, no doctor portal, no two-way clinician workflow — the doctor is a PDF recipient, not a user. [uncertain: exact export format details (PDF vs link) not fully documented in fetched sources]
product.action_loop_monetization: The loop IS the business model: interpretation -> Action Plan (1-5 goals; 7,500+ actions: foods, supplements with dosages, exercise, sleep, mindfulness) -> recipes -> app/text/email reminders -> retest every 3 months ($500-700 repurchase) -> membership renewal $149/yr. Supplements are recommended with dosages but (per current sources) sold via partner/third-party links rather than an owned store [uncertain: current supplement marketplace arrangement]. No telemedicine, no prescriptions, no imaging marketplace. New monetization layer: B2B licensing of the engine (Terra platform, May 2026) to wellness brands, sports orgs, and the US military — margin migrating from D2C kits to platform licensing.

technology.ai_approach: Proprietary engine (historically 'SegterraX') — rules + ML over a curated knowledge base (studies must be 'robust, unambiguous, done on humans'), NOT a general LLM pipeline. InnerAge uses ML weighted regression against its own population dataset. 2024: 'Ask InsideTracker' conversational AI added. 2026: rebranded/platformized as Terra — 'neurosymbolic' hybrid (deep-learning pattern recognition + rule-based symbolic reasoning for 'hallucination-free' output) over 10B+ data points and 7,000+ studies. Human-in-loop: science team (ex-Director of Nutrition) curates content; no clinician reviews individual results.
technology.data_inputs: Blood (Quest panel or uploaded results, up to 48 biomarkers); DNA (261 variants, own kit or $29 upload); wearables/fitness — Apple Health (iOS only), Fitbit, Garmin, Oura Ring (iOS+Android), all one-way ingest of activity/sleep (Oura adds sleep staging, HRV-adjacent metrics); user profile (age, sex, activity, goals 1-5). No CGM, no questionnaire-based risk engines, no pharmacy/claims data.
technology.data_interoperability: Ingestion: own kits, paid upload of external lab results (manual, $119), wearable OAuth APIs. Exhaustion: manual share/download of results for doctors; no write-back to Apple Health (all wearable integrations documented as one-way INTO InsideTracker). No FHIR, no Apple Health Records, no Health Connect, no LIS/API program for consumers — the B2B Terra platform is the first real API surface (partner data + major-lab integration claims). For a BR lens: zero WhatsApp, zero REL/RNDS, PDF-only-in-paid. [uncertain: Terra's lab/wearable integration specifics are press-release level]
technology.platform: Web app (primary) + iOS/Android mobile apps; B2B Terra platform (API/platform-as-a-service for partners).

ux.onboarding: Buy plan -> activate -> print lab order -> Quest visit (5-10 min with appointment) -> results + dashboard in 5-7 business days -> pick goals -> Action Plan. Time-to-value ~1-2 weeks for kits; fast path = Blood Results Upload ($119) turning existing labs into an optimized-zone plan in days. DNA results in <2 weeks. Friction: no cheap entry SKU anymore; mandatory mobile-draw surcharge in several states/Canada.
ux.data_visualization: Every biomarker plotted against its personalized optimal zone with a 3-state color code (red = at risk, yellow = needs work, green = optimized); longitudinal trend charts across retests; InnerAge as a single benchmarkable number vs chronological age with per-biomarker contribution; goal/plan progress tracking in-app. Note: a marker can show 'optimized' (clinical zone) yet still drag InnerAge — two distinct visual vocabularies.
ux.engagement_channel: Retention stack: Action Plan reminders (app push, text, email), retest-every-3-months repurchase rhythm, goal streaks/progress, rich content marketing (InsideGuide blog, podcast), 2024 AI chat (Ask InsideTracker) + food logging (Nutrition DeepDive) to raise daily usage between blood draws. No community layer, no coach, no WhatsApp-class channel — engagement is email/app-mediated and purchase-anchored; classic risk is users going dormant between $500 retests.

trust_gaps.clinical_validation_trust: Strongest-in-class transparency effort, all self-authored: 3 peer-reviewed studies — Scientific Reports (~1,000+ users), PLOS One 2023 (28,000 users, endurance training), PLOS Digital Health 2025 (retrospective longitudinal, 20,000-user real-world cohort, sustained improvements in 43 biomarkers over 4 years, p<0.05) — but authors are Segterra/InsideTracker employees (Blander, Deehan, etc.), design is retrospective (no RCT/control), and independent reviewers flag: no rigorous independent validation of outcomes (Keep Health), and no scientific consensus that 'optimal zones' exist for every biomarker (LiveScience critique). Known bias: reference/InnerAge population is ~85% white, active, normal-BMI, 40-43 — scores degrade for anyone else (InnerBody). Every recommendation links to a cited study (credibility UX win). Science advisory board exists; billing transparency is clean (flat cash prices, HSA/FSA). Risk list: self-validation, population bias, supplement-dosage advice without clinician review, retrospective-only evidence.
trust_gaps.regulatory_posture: Pure US wellness positioning: lifestyle recommendations that 'do not require a doctor', 'before you need medical care' framing; explicit 'not a substitute for a licensed medical professional'; no diagnosis/treatment claims; no FDA device clearance claimed — blood runs through physician-order-eligible CLIA-certified Quest infrastructure [uncertain: exact FDA/CLIA posture inferred from Quest model + disclaimers, not from an official regulatory statement]. HIPAA + SOC2 compliance, PII-stripped research consent opt-in (shareable with NIH). HSA/FSA eligibility signals 'wellness not medical necessity'. Never registered with ANVISA, no LGPD posture — irrelevant to their market but illustrative of the wellness-vs-SaMD line Dr. Exame must respect under RDC 657/2022: InsideTracker stays below the device line by never interpreting toward disease, only toward 'optimization'.
trust_gaps.gaps_opportunities: What they DON'T do (Dr. Exame opportunities): zero family/dependents/pediatric/caregiver depth (single adult accounts, 18+ only); no doctor workflow (no brief, no portal, no SOAP — doctor gets a PDF); no free/cheap PDF ingestion (charge $119 to read your existing labs); no WhatsApp-class engagement channel (US email/app habits only); not available in Brazil (no Quest equivalent, no Portuguese, no PIX-friendly pricing); no CGM integration; no community/coaching; population-biased InnerAge (85% white/fit/40s) — a market of everyone else. What WORKS (inspiration, not copy): the Optimal Zone as the product's signature mental model (reframe 'normal' vs 'ideal' — the single biggest idea Dr. Exame inherits); one aspirational number (InnerAge) as shareable/renews-purpose metric; every recommendation backed by a visible citation; 3-month retest cadence engineered as repurchase loop; publishing outcome studies (even self-authored retrospective) as the credibility moat; 3-state color grammar (at-risk/needs-work/optimized) that lay users instantly read; B2B licensing of the interpretation engine as a second revenue curve.
trust_gaps.relevance: High — InsideTracker is the conceptual ancestor of Dr. Exame's 'valor ideal': it invented the consumer product built on optimal zones vs lab reference ranges, plus the biological-age scorecard (InnerAge 2.0) that Dr. Exame's biometric-profile direction echoes. Study it for the zone grammar, citation-anchored recommendations, and retest-as-subscription economics; beat it on family depth, doctor workflow, Brazil-native ingestion (WhatsApp/PDF-gratis), and pediatric/faixas etárias — the exact pillars where InsideTracker is structurally empty.
